description: handle_mdn_send checks CRLF not just on client-intent fields (subject, textBody, reportingUA) but also on nominally server-set fields (mdnGateway, originalMessageId, originalRecipient, error items). The comment explains why: a client CAN supply these fields in the shared Mdn struct, and any that reach RFC 5322 header generation must be CRLF-clean to prevent header injection. A future contributor might argue 'these are server-set, skip the check' — they would be wrong. The defense is correct and must stay.
title: CRLF injection defense on server-set fields is correct and should be preserved
